CLEAN

No blocking source finding within the requested scope. R5 fences completion through a fresh post-idle actual END observation and retains sampled violations before that fence. This verdict covers the copied observation history. It makes no claim about unsampled in-tick mutations or later world states.

Source anchors below are relative to `/tmp/lodekeeper-station-room-history-r5/source/`. P means `fabric/src/verification/java/dev/lodekeeper/fabric/RuntimeVerification.java`; M means `fabric-modern/src/verification/java/dev/lodekeeper/fabric/modern/RuntimeVerification.java`. PA means `fabric-1211/src/verification/java/dev/lodekeeper/fabric/VerificationApi.java`; MA means the modern `VerificationApi.java` beside M.

The R4 P1 is corrected at P:4234 and M:3760. First observed idle/stopped navigation saves the highest issued request sequence. An outstanding pre-idle request cannot qualify even if its server execution or client delivery happens later. The first strictly newer delivered snapshot pins its server tick and sequence. Acceptance then needs another strictly newer request receipt with `stationHistoryLastEndServerTick > stationRoomCompletionServerFenceTick`. Same-tick polling cannot satisfy that inequality. Missing or malformed fields remain pending. P:4834 and M:4376 reset all fence fields whenever engine or navigation activity is observed; P:4356 and M:3882 reset them at case start. Pending completion fails under the existing 1200-tick bound.

For the R4 counterexample, a saved valid END-200 receipt is excluded by its pre-idle sequence. A support violation sampled at END 201 makes history false. Repair at END 202 cannot restore it. Both post-idle receipts copy that false history, so the final predicate rejects completion. Fence resets change only client scalar fields. They never reset fixture history.

Publication and receipt coherence hold in the inspected paths. P:5984 and M:5751 allow one observation future, increment sequence only when issuing a request, and collect inventory, equipment, cursor, current world fields, health/food/difficulty, and station history in one server-executor task. The captured server thread also owns fixture seeding and END updates. PA:1772 and MA:1813 keep getters read-only; immutable published history accompanies freshly read current fields. CompletableFuture and the client executor deliver the snapshot. Their identity guard rejects displaced callbacks. Snapshot and delivered sequence are assigned together on the client thread at P:6033 and M:5798. Evaluation, fence checks, and addResult execute on that same client thread without an event-loop yield.

P:4261 and M:3787 copy fence values beside the accepted snapshot receipt, including accepted sequence/server tick. P:6225 and M:5931 use that copy in CaseResult; its constructor copies the map again. CAPTURING prevents further evaluation, and subsequent observations cannot alter the saved result. The screenshot callbacks only update screenshot state. No stale/torn pairing was found in these paths.

The R2 sampling and debit-reversal fixes remain. P:987/1004 and M:923/2356 invoke the real Runnable observer from actual END_SERVER_TICK. PA:1963 and MA:2004 require consecutive ticks after authentic seeding. Readiness requires positive END count, clean stock 1, and no debit/placement/removal/return before command dispatch. PA:1972 and MA:2013 retain sticky invalidation for sampled support loss, duplicate furnaces/ordinary stock, pre-placement debit reversal, position change, non-AIR removal, refurnacing, and stock loss after return. First placement records a newly allocated immutable BlockPos once, its first tick, stock 0, and bedrock support. Final ordering retains `debit > initialObserved`, `placed >= debit`, `removed > placed`, and `returned >= removed`, allowing removal and return in one later END.

P:4971 and M:4513 preserve the final ingot 1, raw iron 0 in both counts, health 20, food 20, NORMAL difficulty, empty cursor/equipment, furnace-menu opening, no maintenance, original setup/support, 73-cell census, and bounded 1..2 stone changes. Supported NORMAL completion additionally requires ordinary stock 1, current nearby furnace 0, valid ordered history, and the outer idle/stopped-navigation gates. Current fields are gathered anew for the accepted observation.

Exact version dispatch remains at P:4203 and M:3729. The Object/Runnable seam avoids requiring a new fixture method on older final fixture classes. Existing older APIs were inspected and lack Runnable. Unsupported profiles keep their old path; TUNNEL and APPROACH keep their floor/furnace, stance, air, geometry, inventory, and other predicates. Fence/setup/completion/result helpers and case start match exactly between runtime mirrors. Native fixture/history logic matches after mapping names are normalized. ISSUES

Reviewed the complete frozen patch and state under `/tmp/lodekeeper-station-room-history-r2/`. All baseline and candidate digests match state.json. Applying every patch hunk in memory reconstructs all four candidate files exactly. The four canonical verifier files also matched the frozen candidate when read.

- Manifest SHA-256 `0014b46d514fdf6991fdf00862ae526261ea7e66b58428584234e38ef53fe796`.
- Patch SHA-256 `d24f3c2c72173681d35441e6d9973b34b80fb8f9989d08c3cb7643d36392c413`.
- State SHA-256 `b9f0a7d440384c02fbfe60216b67320ad60fad07b48a352a3f4801ef7c4fb4f8`.
- Recorded baseline `701e658961563c97c8693b6641734fda31b796b7`.

1. P1. History advances only on client-requested snapshots, so intermediate server-tick violations can escape the proof.

   Changed call sites are [primary VerificationApi.java](/tmp/lodekeeper-station-room-history-r2/source/fabric-1211/src/verification/java/dev/lodekeeper/fabric/VerificationApi.java:1874) and [modern VerificationApi.java](/tmp/lodekeeper-station-room-history-r2/source/fabric-modern/src/verification/java/dev/lodekeeper/fabric/modern/VerificationApi.java:1915). Both call `observeHistory` from the receipt getter. Its only runtime caller is `requestObservation`, through `server.execute`, at primary RuntimeVerification.java lines 5903 and 5923, and modern lines 5670 and 5689. Normal station-room observation requests occur every 20 client ticks, at primary lines 461 and 1328, and modern lines 372 and 1236. The actual END_SERVER_TICK hooks at primary lines 985-1030 and modern lines 921 and 2337-2381 contain no station-room observation.

   Capturing the right thread proves server-thread access, but supplies no witness for intervening END_SERVER_TICK states. A duplicate furnace, support loss followed by repair, or removal/replacement between requests never makes `historyValid` false. The next snapshot can accept an apparently intact furnace followed by AIR and returned stock. A short placement can also be missed and cause a false failure. These are source-derived gaps; this review did not reproduce them in a client.

   Minimal fix. Advance the observer in both existing END_SERVER_TICK hooks from fixture seeding onward. Publish an immutable scalar receipt with its actual observation tick. Snapshot getters should copy/read that receipt without advancing history. Keep all identity checks and sticky invalidation. Retain `removed > placed` and `returned >= removed`, so AIR removal and returned stock observed together remain valid. Scope the new observer and proof to the two selected NORMAL profiles.

2. P2. A recorded debit can be reversed before placement without invalidating history.

   The affected branches are [primary VerificationApi.java](/tmp/lodekeeper-station-room-history-r2/source/fabric-1211/src/verification/java/dev/lodekeeper/fabric/VerificationApi.java:1946), lines 1946-1953, and [modern VerificationApi.java](/tmp/lodekeeper-station-room-history-r2/source/fabric-modern/src/verification/java/dev/lodekeeper/fabric/modern/VerificationApi.java:1987), lines 1987-1994. Stock continuity is checked only after `placementTick >= 0`. Before placement, `stock == 1` leaves an earlier debit intact.

   An accepted source trace is initial observation at tick 100 with ordinary stock 1 and no furnace; tick 101 with stock 0 and no furnace; tick 102 with stock 1 and no furnace; tick 103 with stock 0 and one furnace on bedrock at P; tick 104 with stock 1, no furnace, and AIR at P. The receipt retains debit 101, placement 103, removal 104, and return 104, with `historyValid=true`. Both completion helpers accept those ordered ticks. The debit reversal at 102 disappears from the proof even though it was observed. Fixing sampling alone does not fix this branch.

   Minimal fix. Once the first debit is recorded, invalidate any observed return to stock 1 before first placement. Preserve the post-placement checks and the permitted removal/return observation on the same tick. Do not reset the debit or recover from an invalid history.

The remaining inspected requirements are preserved in the frozen patch. Fixture construction follows native seeding of one ordinary furnace on the server executor. Player, world, server, and thread identities are pinned. The first position is a newly allocated immutable BlockPos and is assigned once, with first placement tick and bedrock witness. Observed duplicate stock/furnaces, changed position, support loss, non-AIR removal, refurnacing after removal, and stock loss after return stickily invalidate history. Receipt data are strings returned through Map.copyOf. The additions contain no native effect calls or reflection.

Case start captures an immutable baseline before the command. Completion requires valid initial history, zero placement/removal/return state, debit -1, ordinary stock 1, and debit later than the initial observation. Exact version dispatch confines the new final predicate to 1.21.1/26.3 NORMAL. Older profiles retain current furnace/floor checks. TUNNEL and APPROACH retain their current stance, air, geometry, floor, furnace inventory, and other legacy predicates. Current health 20, food, difficulty, menu opening, cursor, equipment, raw iron, one ingot, 73 candidate cells, bounded 1..2 stone changes, support, no maintenance, and outer idle/stopped-navigation gates remain. Primary and modern history code match after mapping names are normalized. Existing case limits remain 1200 ticks.

The supplied 14c native JSON confirms the stale final assertion after one ingot, zero raw iron, returned furnace 1, changed stone 2, full health, empty cursor, idle/stopped navigation, and zero nearby furnaces. Its sibling latest.log line 182 records OWNED_STATION_RECOVERED at -1,64,0. The runner receipt records unchanged production jar, no class-provenance violations, and a 180-second limit. Its cleanup gate was optional. Each new focused run must independently use existing `--require-station-cleanup`, which requires OWNED_STATION_RECOVERED and rejects OWNED_STATION_LEFT. History alone cannot prove ownership.

Local javap verified the new tick, world, inventory, component-equality, and position APIs in cached exact 1.21.1/26.3 jars. This is source and symbol review only. The supplied r1 build results are not r2 build or runtime proof. No build, test, client, Git operation, restart, source change, or nested agent was performed. Only this report was written. The pstack Prove It Works principle led to direct hash, patch, lifecycle, and receipt inspection. Throughput checkpoint is n/a for read-only investigation. HOLD.

ISSUES

P1. Completion can reuse a valid pre-idle snapshot after an actual END observation has invalidated history.

The affected new completion checks are [primary RuntimeVerification.java](/tmp/lodekeeper-station-room-history-r4/source/fabric/src/verification/java/dev/lodekeeper/fabric/RuntimeVerification.java:4246) and [modern RuntimeVerification.java](/tmp/lodekeeper-station-room-history-r4/source/fabric-modern/src/verification/java/dev/lodekeeper/fabric/modern/RuntimeVerification.java:3772). Both compare `lastEndTick == observed` inside the saved receipt. Neither checks that this receipt includes the END observations through command completion.

Primary lines 1334-1340 and modern lines 1236-1249 request snapshots every 20 client ticks, then evaluate the current case using `latestSnapshot`. Requesting a snapshot does not wait for its replacement. Primary lines 3171-3176 and modern lines 4637-4641 route every client evaluation into the prepared-safety predicate. The outer idle/stopped gates at primary lines 4782-4787 and modern lines 4324-4329 do not fence the observation sequence or request a post-idle receipt. The final station branches at primary lines 4913-4934 and modern lines 4455-4476 consume that saved snapshot.

A source-derived counterexample follows. Seed and initial readiness are clean. Placement, later AIR removal, and ordinary return occur in order. A snapshot S containing END 200 records valid completed history, ordinary stock 1, nearby furnace 0, one ingot, zero raw iron, and all remaining final guards. The client engine is still waiting for its recovery confirmation. At actual END 201, bedrock under the recorded station position is missing. The observer sets `historyValid=false`. END 202 sees repaired support and retains false. The client then becomes idle with stopped navigation and uses S before receiving another snapshot. S still says valid, with historical last-END and observed tick both 200. The verifier passes and enters CAPTURING. Further evaluation returns early in that state. An actual OWNED_STATION_RECOVERED log and no LEFT log can still satisfy the separate runner gate.

This gap concerns a violation sampled at END. It does not rely on a mutation hidden between END observations. The observer captures the violation correctly, but completion can discard it by accepting an older receipt. This trace was inferred from the source, not reproduced in a client.

Minimal fix. For supported NORMAL station-room cases, establish a completion fence when idle and stopped navigation are first observed. Request a new server observation and require its sequence to follow that fence. Require the copied history to include an actual END observation after the server-side fence before evaluating completion. Keep snapshot getters read-only and preserve every current guard. An outstanding request issued before idle must not satisfy the fence. Keep older profiles, TUNNEL, and APPROACH on their existing paths.

Frozen-input verification passed. I read the complete patch and state, checked each archived baseline and candidate digest, and reconstructed every candidate from the patch in memory. All four canonical files under `/Users/luinbytes/src/lodekeeper` matched r4. All four baseline files also matched the retained r2 baseline and the corresponding entries in the 14c artifact source manifest.

- Manifest SHA-256 `a066c0f63f0c42f077865bfa73553230acc824e382be367b0490d4ef0514ba05`.
- Patch SHA-256 `425f55853f61bf491dcd10ad69ce973bf66c9e0c0b23ae69cc7ec04a709571c1`.
- State SHA-256 `506a5c911920af79ec0324477d3cd32f02044f1c9add0f5c5d2afdf0422a7196`.
- Prior r2 review SHA-256 `1813bb7dd5f0598c0c0ef115c12a280a754c1af6bce18f2af68b370c0f934c93`.
- Recorded baseline `701e658961563c97c8693b6641734fda31b796b7`. Commit membership was not independently checked through Git.

The r2 P1 observation-call gap is corrected. Primary has one END registration at line 985 and one observer call at line 1002. Modern has one registration at line 921 and one observer call at line 2354. `observeServerMenu` has no additional caller. Seeding occurs on the native server executor after clearing inventory, restoring health/food, selecting NORMAL difficulty, and inserting the ordinary furnace. Seeding publishes count-zero history. `run()` requires consecutive native ticks from seed onward, increments the count, and publishes the new immutable map. Getter calls collect fresh world and ordinary-stock fields without advancing history.

No torn scalar publication was found. Fixture construction, END updates, and getter reads share the captured server thread. The history map is immutable. ServerSnapshot copies its maps, then CompletableFuture and the client executor deliver the snapshot. The finding above concerns receipt freshness after this delivery.

The r2 P2 debit reversal is corrected at primary VerificationApi.java line 1979 and modern line 2020. An observed nonzero stock after debit and before placement invalidates history permanently. Both fixture classes match after native API names are normalized. Player, world, server, thread, and native player-list membership are pinned. First placement uses one immutable BlockPos with its first tick and bedrock witness. Observed duplicate stock/furnaces, changed position, support loss, non-AIR removal, refurnacing, and stock loss after return invalidate history. Removal and return on the same END remain permitted through `removed > placed` and `returned >= removed`.

Readiness requires positive END count, clean initial history, and current ordinary stock 1 before sending the command. The initial receipt is copied before the send. Final checks require increased END count, ordered ticks, exact ordinary stock 1, and current nearby furnace 0. Dispatch limits their use to exact 1.21.1/26.3 NORMAL cases. The Object/Runnable seam adds no method requirement to older fixtures. Existing legacy floor/furnace predicates and TUNNEL/APPROACH stance, air, geometry, floor, furnace-inventory predicates remain. Initial/final health 20, food, difficulty, cursor, equipment, raw/ingot, menu, 73-cell census, bounded 1..2 changes, support, no-maintenance, outer idle/stopped guards, and 1200-tick limit remain. Added history code contains no reflection, ACK injection, or native effect calls.

The focused script admits only prepared_station_room for primary/modern, requests existing `--require-station-cleanup`, uses 180 seconds, and stops on first failure. The runner requires RECOVERED and rejects any LEFT. The original 14c failed JSON and retained repository evidence still report failure. The native log records RECOVERED at line 182. Both frozen 14c jars match their manifest, and the six manifest-listed production source files retain their 14c digests.

Cached exact 1.21.1/26.3 jars confirm the native tick, membership, world, ordinary-component equality, and BlockPos APIs. This is source and symbol review only. R2 compile results do not prove r4 compilation or runtime behavior. No build, test, client, restart, Git operation, nested agent, or source change was performed. Only this report was written. The pstack Prove It Works principle led to direct frozen-input and receipt inspection rather than carrying forward prior PASS claims. Throughput checkpoint is n/a for read-only investigation. HOLD.
